messages:
maria: ran an nsys + perfetto trace on the 8xA100 batch-3 run — uploaded timeline + proto: https://perf.redwood/local/1759004128/nsys (perfetto proto attached)
perf-bot: nsys trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood/local/1759004128/nsys?view=timeline
maria: quick summary: kernel launches look normal, but NVTX is everywhere (per-op) so the trace is basically noise. CPU-side scheduling jitter spikes correspond to thousands of tiny nvtx push/pop calls.
aj: can you repro with NVTX off to show the overhead?
maria: yep. disabled NVTX and reran same workload: host CPU time down ~22%, trace file size down ~6x. KV cache hotspots remain but are far easier to read without op-level NVTX clutter.
tyler: that matches my intuition — we instrumented at too fine a granularity. proposal: switch to per-request and per-batch ranges + a few phase ranges (kv_lookup, scoring, decode, postprocess). e.g. push a range named: "r:<shortid>|b:<n>" around the main batch loop, and only annotate big phases inside.
sasha: +1. also: never put full request bodies or full uuids in labels (PII & huge strings). use a short hashed prefix (fnv1a/base64) plus a per-process salt: e.g. "r:h1b2|m:llama70b|p:kv"
aj: naming should be compact for perfetto search. propose pattern: "r:<id>|m:<model>|p:<phase>|b:<batch>" — short keys, consistent. avoid spaces and long human sentences.
maria: perf note: NVTX label handling itself allocates/copies strings on the host in our current helper. that string churn is a measurable cost at high qps. grouping reduces string churn massively.
tyler: another mitigation: sampling. full op-level NVTX for 1% of requests, batch-level for all requests. keeps fidelity for debugging without 99% overhead.
sasha: sampling+group spans seems like the right default. make full op-level NVTX an env flag for local debugging or ses­sion-level tracing.
aj: for kernel selection visibility, emit lightweight markers only at decision points: before_select_kernel(); after_select_kernel(chosen_id, qpath). include kernel id + quant path (q4_0,q5_1). avoid instrumenting every operator invocation unless you're debugging a kernel bug.
maria: toy C++ helper (avoid allocations, fixed buffer):

```cpp
// very small non-allocating NVTX label helper
struct NVLabel { char buf[64]; };
NVLabel make_label(const char* req_hash, int batch, const char* phase){
  // snprintf into buf, but avoid std::string / heap allocs
  // result examples: "r:h3f|b:3|p:kv" (max 64 bytes)
}
// usage in hot loop:
NVLabel lbl = make_label(req_hash, batch, "kv");
nvtxRangePushEx(&attr_with_color, lbl.buf);
// work
nvtxRangePop();
```

We should forbid std::string allocations inside the hot path helpers. keep labels <=64 chars; perfetto truncates long names anyway.
tyler: limit length + reuse buffers per thread. also cap number of nested ranges to avoid stack allocation blowups.
sasha: ran a quick experiment: op-level NVTX vs batch-level NVTX on same job: op-level increased host CPU ~+35% and produced ~12GB trace; batch-level increased host CPU ~+6% and produced ~1.8GB trace. KV lookup hotspots were visible in both traces.
aj: nsys tip for CI collection: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output trace.nsys-rep --sample=cpu --force-overwrite` and upload proto + a condensed JSON summary to perf store. for perfetto, keep the proto and also export a light JSON with aggregated ranges.
maria: follow-ups I can action:
- add a compact, non-allocating label helper (tyler to implement)
- add NVTX_LEVEL env: {off,batch,op,sampled} (config in runtime)
- add hashed req id utility + per-process salt (sasha)
- add kernel-selection markers only (aj)
- add tests that assert no heap allocs in hot NVTX helpers
I'll open a small PR tomorrow with the helper + basic tests.
aj: please also document the naming convention and default NVTX_LEVEL in eng-runtime/README and in the perf runbooks so infra/perf folks know what to expect.
maria: will add a short section and example commands. will also include recommended nsys/perfetto CLI flags and the sampling guidance.
tyler: one more: consider tagging ranges with a tiny numeric code in addition to text name for faster parsing by tooling (e.g. attach attr->domainId = 42). text is human-friendly but avoid making tooling parse long strings.
sasha: good idea — domainId / color enums are cheap. we can keep both (compact text + integer tag).
maria: ok that's our plan. thanks all :rocket:
